summary.text: Saint Sophronius was a monk, writer, and Patriarch of Jerusalem who opposed teachings that diminished Christ’s human activity or human will.

blocks.text: Born in Damascus around 560, he received a classical education before seeking monastic life. With John Moschus he visited monasteries and collected accounts of ascetics. Those encounters stand behind the Spiritual Meadow tradition.

blocks.text: Wars displaced him through Palestine, Egypt, and Rome. He eventually became Patriarch of Jerusalem. His final ministry coincided with the siege and surrender of Jerusalem, placing the local Christian community under new political rule.
blocks.locator: Paragraphs on travel, patriarchate and the siege of Jerusalem

blocks.text: In 633 he opposed monoenergism, the teaching that Christ has only one divine-human activity. As patriarch he also opposed monothelitism, which asserts only one will in Christ. His resistance helped prepare the later defense of Christ’s fully divine and fully human willing.
blocks.locator: Paragraphs on Sophronius’s appeal to Cyrus and his Jerusalem patriarchate

blocks.text: The Saint’s life describes his grief during Jerusalem’s ordeal and records his death without a martyr’s execution. The OCA’s Church History gives 638; its separate Saint’s life prints a different terminal date for his patriarchate.
